statement: A running model, not a calibrated one. The sizes of its leaves, flower, leaf stalk and seed head, the length of its stems, the months it flowers in and the summer fall of its old leaves are from floras, plant records and nurseries of Clematis cirrhosa and of this cultivar; the stiffness of its shoots is a congener’s (Clematis flammula) and their reach is bounded by a published study of searcher shoots. Its rates of growth, how freely it branches and flowers, how much seed it sets and every date inside those months are assumptions chosen to agree with what those records say of a plant’s size and season. How a shoot chooses its way over a structure, and how a stem shares its thickening where it branches, are still thinner than the wisteria model those ten numbers are copied from. None has been measured on a plant. Use its output to compare scenarios and to show what a design implies, not to predict dates, sizes or loads.

names.basis: Two leaf forms, from Flora of Turkey (as reproduced at https://turkiyebitkileri.com/): long shoots usually bear ternate leaves, whose stalks twine, and that is the ordinary leaf here; short-shoot leaves are simple, deeply toothed to almost entire, and are named "short_shoot". The flowers stand in the leaf axils on stalks 2 to 5 cm long (Flora Europaea) and are "nodding" (https://www.cretanflora.com/clematis_cirrhosa_text.html; Clematis on the Web): the stalk stands out from its node and the flower hangs from the end of it. The direction given with a flower is therefore the way its stalk runs out from the node, not the way the flower faces; the drawing turns the bell down from the end of the stalk. That the seed head is carried on the same stalk in the same way is assumed: no source says how it is held.

phenology.budburstDoy.basis: New shoots are taken to start in mid March, as the flowers finish (RHS: flowers late autumn to early spring). No dated source for the start of growth.

phenology.growthEndDoy.basis: Extension is taken to end in mid October. A nursery that grows it says it rests in summer heat, browning or dropping some leaves in July and August of a hot dry year, and that fresh growth returns in September (https://www.ashridgetrees.co.uk/clematis-cirrhosa-freckles). The engine spreads a season’s growth as one hump between two dates, so the rest itself is not modelled; the date only lets autumn growth happen. Not measured.

phenology.leafFlushDoy.basis: New leaves open with the new shoots, from late March. Placed after bud break; no dated source.

phenology.autumnColourDoy.basis: Not applicable to this plant: it is evergreen (RHS) and no leaf of it reads these days. Its leaves are "tinged bronze in winter" (RHS), which the model cannot yet show; the days stand where that bronzing would begin.

phenology.leafFallDoy.basis: Not applicable to this plant: it is evergreen (RHS) and no leaf of it reads these days; a leaf goes when its seasons are up (organs.leafLifespanYears). Present because every model carries every parameter.

phenology.floralInitiationDoy.basis: RHS pruning group 1: it flowers "on shoots produced the previous summer" (https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/clematis/group-one-pruning-guide). Buds are taken to form in the first half of September, when growth picks up after the summer rest, so that they show in October. The dates are not from a source.

phenology.flowerOpenDoy.basis: Flowers open from 25 October to 14 February, a window that runs through the new year. A nursery that grows it gives November to February, with first flowers sometimes in late October on a sunny south-facing wall (https://www.ashridgetrees.co.uk/clematis-cirrhosa-freckles); "most flowers start in November" (https://internationalclematissociety.org/?p=742); the RHS gives late autumn to early spring. The days themselves are chosen inside that envelope, not dated on a plant.

phenology.petalFallDoy.basis: The end of the RHS flowering envelope, in the following year (14 February to 21 March). Not read while phenology.flowerLastsDays is set, which gives each flower its own last day.

phenology.flowerLastsDays.basis: No source gives how long one flower lasts. A flower record stands for the flowers of one leaf axil, "solitary or in pairs" (https://www.treesandshrubsonline.org/articles/clematis/clematis-cirrhosa/), which follow one another: three to six weeks. With openings from late October to mid February this carries the display into early March, the end of the RHS envelope (late autumn to early spring).

extension.leaderMPerSeason.basis: RHS: 2.5 to 4 m in 2 to 5 years; Bean: vigorous, "needs ample space"; rate of growth "average" in the trade. A size band is not a growth rate: 1.6 m a season, with the slower first two seasons below, brings a stem to 2.5 m in its second year and to its length in its third, inside the RHS band. Not measured.

extension.lateralMPerSeasonByOrder.basis: Scaled down from the leader rate by branch order. Not measured.

extension.whipMPerSeason.basis: Every year the older stems throw long new shoots from their nodes; these carry the leaves and next winter’s flowers. As fast as a first-order branch. Not measured.

extension.establishmentFactorByYear.basis: Slower while it roots in: half speed in the planting year, four fifths in the next. Assumed; no source.

architecture.trunkStemStartYears.basis: Four stems from the nursery plant in the first season, and more from the base in each of the next three: the RHS advises cutting a newly planted clematis to a strong pair of buds about 30 cm above the soil to make it throw several stems (https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/clematis/group-one-pruning-guide). Ten stems by the fourth season is chosen so that a trained plant covers its support in the two to five years the RHS gives for its full size (2.5 to 4 m, https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/89092/clematis-cirrhosa-var-purpurascens-freckles-c/details). Not counted on a plant.

architecture.nurseryCaneM.basis: Sold in 3-litre pots (https://www.ashridgetrees.co.uk/clematis-cirrhosa-freckles); such a plant is commonly tied to a cane of about 0.6 m. Not measured.

architecture.maxBranchOrder.basis: Clematis branch freely from the opposite buds at each node; three orders of branch above the main stems are allowed. A limit of the model, not an observation.

architecture.leaderLengthM.basis: International Clematis Society: a vigorous evergreen climber that "grows 3-4 metres long". Used as the length a main stem reaches, measured along the stem. RHS gives a height of 2.5 to 4 m; Clematis on the Web 4 to 5 m.

architecture.lateralLengthMByOrder.basis: Scaled down from the main stems by branch order. Not measured.

architecture.lateralLengthSpread.basis: Branches of one order are taken to vary by three tenths either way in length. Assumed; no source.

architecture.lateralChanceByParentOrder.basis: A clematis stem trained along a support breaks into side stems from the opposite buds at nearly every place where the support forks, a little less readily on higher orders. Chosen so that the plant fills its support in the two to five years the RHS gives; no count on a plant.

architecture.budExtraDormancyChance.basis: About a third of the buds that will make a side stem wait a year or two before they break, so the framework fills in over several years and not all at once. Assumed.

architecture.maxStemsPerRoute.basis: The stems are slender and wiry, a few millimetres thick for years, and run several together along one wire or lath, clasping one another: eight are let share a member before the next looks elsewhere, so that a trained plant fills its support thickly. Assumed.

architecture.maxStemsPerPrimaryMember.basis: Two more than on a lath or cable: a glulam member is wide enough to tie more of these slender stems to. Assumed.

routing.occupancyCost.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.downhillCostPerM.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.uphillBonusPerM.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.straightOnBonus.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.riserBonus.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.tierBonus.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.roleDropChance.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.noise.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.giveUpCost.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

attachment.maxGraspDiameterMm.basis: No measurement exists. The leaf stalk that does the clasping is 13 to 38 mm long in the species (Bean), and a stalk has to go once round what it holds: that is a support 4 to 12 mm thick, taken here as 8 mm. A 5 mm cable qualifies, a 40 mm lath does not, and on timber the plant has to be tied.

attachment.minPitchM.basis: Not applicable to this plant: its stems do not twine, they lie along the support and the leaf stalks hold it. Present because every model carries every parameter.

attachment.pitchPerCircumference.basis: Not applicable to this plant: see attachment.minPitchM.

organs.leafSpacingM.basis: Distance between the pairs of leaves on a long shoot. No flora gives it; in the photograph of the species on canes listed in morphology.json ("Clematis cirrhosa, jardí botànic de València.JPG") the pairs stand about a leaf’s length or less apart on the leafy shoots. 4 to 6 cm is taken; the engine lays nodes on stem points 4 cm apart. To be measured on a plant.

organs.leafLengthM.basis: Stalk and blade together, of the ternate leaf of a long shoot: Bean gives the stalk as 1/2 to 1 1/2 in. (1.3 to 3.8 cm, https://www.treesandshrubsonline.org/articles/clematis/clematis-cirrhosa/), the Cretan Flora the leaflets as 2 to 5 cm (https://www.cretanflora.com/clematis_cirrhosa_text.html), and the end leaflet stands on a stalk of its own of about a fifth of its length (read from the photographs listed in morphology.json). Their sum is about 3.7 to 9.8 cm, of which 5.5 to 9.5 cm is used, the upper part because the photographs of the cultivar show ternate leaves near the size of its flowers (5 to 7.5 cm). Not measured on the cultivar.

organs.leavesPerNode.basis: Leaves opposite: in pairs at each node, as in all clematis.

organs.spurChance.basis: No spurs: this plant flowers from the leaf axils of last summer’s shoots, not on short woody spurs of the wisteria kind.

organs.spurLengthM.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

organs.spurLeafCount.basis: No spurs are modelled for this plant.

organs.racemeLengthM.basis: The width of one open flower. International Clematis Society, of this cultivar: flowers "5-7.5 cm across", the four sepals "3-4 cm long and 2-2.5 cm wide". Flora Europaea gives 4 to 7 cm for the species. The RHS record’s "to 10cm in width" and its Award of Garden Merit description’s "5cm wide" disagree with each other; the Society’s figure lies between them and agrees with the sepal length.

organs.whipShareOfNodes.basis: Three older nodes in twenty throw a long shoot each year. Assumed: chosen with organs.whipsPerYearMax so that an established plant makes several tens of long shoots a year and covers its support within the two to five years the RHS gives, which a plant described as "vigorous" that "needs ample space" (Bean, https://www.treesandshrubsonline.org/articles/clematis/clematis-cirrhosa/) and that reaches 4 m by 1.5 m (Crocus, https://www.crocus.co.uk/plants/_/clematis-cirrhosa-var-purpurascens-freckles/classid.872/) must do. Where they find no support they hang in curtains.

organs.whipsPerYearMax.basis: A cap on new long shoots a year. Assumed; see organs.whipShareOfNodes.

organs.whipLengthM.basis: Length of a year’s long shoot from an older stem. No length is published; up to 1.5 m in a season is assumed for a plant that is "vigorous" (Bean) and grows 3 to 4 m long (International Clematis Society). Where it finds no support it arches and hangs under its own weight (mechanics.*).

organs.leafLifespanYears.basis: Evergreen (RHS). How long a leaf lives is not published. A leaf is taken to live through the season it is made in and the next, through two winters, and to fall in the summer rest of the year after (phenology.evergreenLeafFallDoy): in the wild the species "can aestivate through hot dry summers by shedding its foliage" (Bean, https://www.treesandshrubsonline.org/articles/clematis/clematis-cirrhosa/), and in British gardens leaves may brown or partly drop in July and August of a hot dry year (https://www.ashridgetrees.co.uk/clematis-cirrhosa-freckles), which in an ordinary British summer is taken to take only the oldest. One season was tried and left the plant much thinner in winter than an evergreen described as glossy and dense. Not measured.

organs.clearStemHeightM.basis: The lowest quarter metre of the stems is taken to carry no side growth: old evergreen clematis are bare at the base. Assumed.

flowering.competenceYears.basis: A nursery plant of this size is of flowering age and is taken to flower, lightly, in its first winter after a spring planting. Assumed.

flowering.maturityRamp.basis: Fewer flowers while it establishes: four tenths of full in the first winter, eight tenths in the second. Assumed.

flowering.spurFloralChance.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

flowering.unprunedFactor.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

flowering.currentSeasonFlowersPerM.basis: Flower sites for each metre of the summer’s long-shoot growth, opening the following winter: RHS group 1 flowers "on shoots produced the previous season" (https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/clematis/group-one-pruning-guide). With the flowering short shoots (sideShoots.terminalFlowerShare) this gives several hundred flowers a winter on an established plant, as a garden record of "hundreds of flowers and buds" on a wall plant in December has it (https://fobssheffield.co.uk/plant-of-the-month/clematis-cirrhosa-freckles). The rate is not from a count.

flowering.currentSeasonMinShootM.basis: A shoot that has made less than 15 cm in the year is taken not to flower. Assumed.

pruning.summerLeavesKept.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

pruning.winterBudsKept.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

regrowth.shootsPerCut.basis: A cut clematis stem shoots from the pair of buds at the node below the cut: one or two shoots. It "can be cut back to 1 metre" after flowering (https://internationalclematissociety.org/?p=742). The number is assumed.

thickening.tipRadiusSquaredMm2.basis: A young shoot about 2 mm thick (radius 1 mm): the stems are "woody, slender" (https://www.cretanflora.com/clematis_cirrhosa_text.html). An estimate, not a measurement.

thickening.radiusSquaredPerMetreMm2.basis: Thin, wiry stems that thicken slowly: with this a main stem that carries 40 m of growth is about 14 mm thick at the base. No measurement of an old plant was found.

thickening.branchShare.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

fruit.setShare.basis: Six flower sites in ten are taken to leave a seed head. The cultivar is described as having "good silky seed-heads" (RHS Award of Garden Merit description) that "remain on the plant for long periods" (https://www.plantdelights.com/products/clematis-cirrhosa-freckles), and its flowers are visited by bees in winter (RHS Plants for Pollinators); how many set in Britain is not published.

fruit.lengthM.basis: One achene with its feathered tail, which is what the model’s unit of length is: the head is a ball of them. Bean: seed-vessels "terminated by plumose styles 1 1/2 to 2 in. long, forming large, beautifully silky tassels" (3.8 to 5.1 cm); the achene itself is 3 to 5 mm (https://www.cretanflora.com/clematis_cirrhosa_text.html). The two added.

fruit.swellDays.basis: The styles lengthen into tails in the weeks after the tepals fall: four to six weeks is assumed. No dated source.

fruit.ripenDoy.basis: The heads are taken to dry from silky green-silver to pale fluff between mid March and mid May. The sources say only that silky seedheads follow the flowers (RHS). No dated source.

fruit.fallDoy.basis: The feathered achenes are taken to blow away between late May and mid July: the seed heads "remain on the plant for long periods after flowering" (Plant Delights). No dated source.

appendages.tendrilNodePattern.basis: No tendrils: it climbs "by twining leaf-stalks" (RHS, of the genus), and the floras describe none.

appendages.leafStalkCoilShare.basis: On a stretch the plant holds by itself, six nodes in ten are taken to have a leaf stalk wound round the support. That the stalks do this is published ("petioles twining" on long shoots, Flora of Turkey; old petioles "indurate, twisting and clasping", https://www.cretanflora.com/clematis_cirrhosa_text.html); the share is not.

appendages.leafStalkLengthM.basis: Bean, of the species: leaf "stalks 1/2 to 1 1/2 in. long". In metres. The cultivar’s own has not been measured.

appendages.aerialRootPatchSpacingM.basis: No clinging rootlets: it climbs by its leaf stalks, and the floras describe none.

appendages.prickleSpacingM.basis: Unarmed: no flora or plant record read describes prickles or thorns on it.

sideShoots.bearingWoodAgeYears.basis: Stems made last year and earlier bear short shoots in their leaf axils. Flora of Turkey distinguishes the long shoots, with ternate leaves and twining stalks, from short shoots with simple leaves (as reproduced at https://turkiyebitkileri.com/); the flowers stand "in the axils of clustered leaves" (https://www.cretanflora.com/clematis_cirrhosa_text.html). That a short shoot appears in the spring after its node was made is assumed.

sideShoots.perMetrePerYear.basis: Short shoots in the leaf axils of last year’s and older stems: the flowers stand "in the axils of clustered leaves" (https://www.cretanflora.com/clematis_cirrhosa_text.html), and Flora of Turkey sets the short shoots with simple leaves apart from the long shoots. Twenty a metre a year is asked for; the engine places no more than the nodes allow. Assumed: no count exists.

sideShoots.lengthM.basis: A short shoot is a cluster of leaves on a few centimetres of stem ("clustered leaves", Cretan Flora). The engine lays leaf nodes on stem points 4 cm apart, so 8 to 20 cm gives each shoot two to five pairs of leaves. Longer than on the plant: a limit of the model, stated in the species profile.

sideShoots.lifespanYears.basis: A short shoot is taken to stay, leafing each year, for three growing seasons before it is shed. Assumed.

sideShoots.terminalFlowerShare.basis: Half the short shoots end in a flower in a year. The flowers stand "in the axils of clustered leaves", solitary or paired (https://www.cretanflora.com/clematis_cirrhosa_text.html), which is what the short shoots are. The share is not from a count.

phenology.evergreenLeafFallDoy.basis: Old leaves fall between mid June and the end of August of the year after their last season: the summer rest in which, a nursery says, the leaves may brown or partly drop in July and August of a hot dry year, with fresh growth around September (https://www.ashridgetrees.co.uk/clematis-cirrhosa-freckles; Thorncroft: a natural dormant period in mid summer, https://www.thorncroftclematis.co.uk/cirrhosa). The window is widened a fortnight earlier to spread the fall. Not dated on a plant.

organs.sideShootLeafLengthM.basis: The simple leaf of a short shoot, stalk and blade together: Bean gives blades 3/4 to 2 in. and stalks 1/2 to 1 1/2 in. (https://www.treesandshrubsonline.org/articles/clematis/clematis-cirrhosa/); the lower part of their sum is taken, since a short-shoot leaf is smaller than the ternate leaf of a long shoot. Not measured on the cultivar.

organs.sideShootLeafSpacingM.basis: The leaves of a short shoot are "clustered" (Cretan Flora): close together. The engine places nodes on stem points 4 cm apart, so anything under 4 cm reads as one node to a stem point.

organs.sideShootLeavesPerNode.basis: Leaves opposite, on short shoots as on long ones (Cretan Flora).

organs.leafTurnToOpenShare.basis: Read from photographs of the plant on canes and on a frame (Wikimedia Commons "Clematis cirrhosa, jardí botànic de València.JPG"; "Clématite Cirrhosa Freckles.jpg"): most blades face out from the support, few lie against it. Not measured.

sideShoots.branchAngleDeg.basis: Short shoots and long shoots leave the stem from the leaf axil at a wide angle, as in the photographs cited under organs.leafTurnToOpenShare. Not measured.

sideShoots.breakSpreadDays.basis: The season’s side shoots break over about five weeks after bud break. Assumed.

sideShoots.startTowardsLight.basis: A shoot sets out a little turned towards up and the light. Assumed.

organs.alternateDivergenceDeg.basis: Not used for its own purpose: the leaves are opposite (Cretan Flora). Opposite pairs of clematis stand at right angles to the pair below (decussate), so 90 is given for where successive nodes place their shoots round the stem. Decussate arrangement is the rule in the genus, not stated for this species.

sideShoots.baseDiameterMm.basis: A short shoot a little thinner at its base than a young long shoot (thickening.tipRadiusSquaredMm2, about 2 mm). Not measured.

mechanics.woodModulusMPa.basis: Of a congener, not this plant: Isnard, Rowe and Speck 2003 measured a structural Young’s modulus of 1.619 GN/m2 (1619 MPa) in the aerial, trellis-forming shoots of Clematis flammula var. maritima, another Mediterranean evergreen-leaved clematis. Taken for set wood of this one.

mechanics.greenShootModulusMPa.basis: Of a congener, not this plant: Isnard, Rowe and Speck 2003 measured 0.855 GN/m2 in the emergent axes of Clematis flammula var. maritima and 1.619 in its trellis-forming shoots. The soft growing end is taken to be softer than either, about half the emergent figure.

mechanics.woodSetDays.basis: A new stretch of these slender shoots is taken to stiffen over about six weeks. Not measured.

mechanics.leafFreshMassPerAreaKgM2.basis: The leaves are "subcoriaceous" (Flora of Turkey) and glossy: a little heavier than a thin leaf, for the engine’s disc 0.56 of the leaf’s length across. Not weighed.

mechanics.inflorescenceFreshMassKg.basis: One bell of four tepals 3 to 4 cm long (International Clematis Society) with its stalk, taken as two grams. Not weighed.

mechanics.fruitFreshMassKg.basis: A head of small dry achenes with feathered tails: half a gram. Not weighed.

mechanics.searcherReachM.basis: Hattermann and others 2022 measured the reach of searcher shoots in 29 climbers, among them Clematis vitalba, which they group with the tendril climbers for its twining leaf stalks: that group and the one root climber reached 0.14 to 0.91 m. This plant’s shoots are slenderer than C. vitalba’s ("woody, slender", Cretan Flora); half a metre is taken inside the range. Not measured on this plant.

attachment.graspReachM.basis: It takes hold with its leaf stalks, which are 1.3 to 3.8 cm long (Bean): a support within about the length of a stalk of the shoot’s tip can be caught. Not measured.
